demonstrations.title: GPU Instancing — Browser WebGPU Proof
demonstrations.summary: A standalone browser sample for adjusting 1,000–50,000 procedural triangle instances, observer offset, and motion.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: It explores how large populations can share one instanced draw call while near and far cohorts update at different cadences.
demonstrations.status: Runnable proof — local sample; not hosted by WebPage
demonstrations.whatItProves: A browser WebGPU instancing experiment and a visible starting point for evaluating population rendering and update cadence.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: A native .NET IVisualizerBackend, Renderer Event Horizon integration, FSM_API/FSM_COS scheduling, compute-to-render, production performance, or a controlled benchmark. The FPS display is an estimate.
demonstrations.runInstructions: From the TheSingularityWorkshop.Visualize repository root, run `py -m http.server 8080`, then open `http://localhost:8080/samples/WebGpuInstancingProof/` in a WebGPU-capable browser. This sample is not currently hosted by WebPage.
demonstrations.requirements: A checkout containing samples/WebGpuInstancingProof, Python's static server, and a browser with WebGPU support.

demonstrations.title: Native WPF / Direct3D 12 Surface Proof
demonstrations.summary: A technical walkthrough of the exploratory native WPF surface, device and queue setup, swapchain presentation, resizing, and resource lifecycle.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: It explores the boundary between a native desktop host and Direct3D 12 presentation without claiming that the full renderer exists.
demonstrations.whatItProves: The exploratory native surface setup and lifecycle represented in the source.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: Geometry rendering, a selected production backend, a real hardware performance result, or a complete Visualize implementation.
demonstrations.runInstructions: This is a native application proof, not a browser demo. Inspect the source; no verified public executable or runtime capture is currently provided.
demonstrations.requirements: Native Windows/WPF and Direct3D 12 development environment for local investigation.

demonstrations.title: Event Horizon Buckets — Renderer Architecture
demonstrations.summary: Explore processing buckets that refresh at different rates, retain valid cached output, and invalidate dependent results when source data changes.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: It addresses the cost of updating every representation at the same frequency, while keeping cache validity and dependency propagation explicit.
demonstrations.whatItProves: The bucket model, dependency propagation, cache-validity rules, representation handoff contracts, membership indexing, and tests in the referenced work.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: A complete spatial partitioner, a full production rendering pipeline, actual GPU execution, or measured end-to-end frame-rate gains.
demonstrations.runInstructions: Review the pull request and its tests. WebPage presents this as an explanatory architecture model; it does not simulate or report performance measurements.
demonstrations.requirements: No special browser capability is required to read the explanation. Renderer source and tests are required to inspect implementation evidence.

demonstrations.title: Singularity City — Digitens Living-World Slice
demonstrations.summary: Explore the current Digiten identity/place model, city topics, and the boundary between authored demonstration data and future autonomous routines.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: A city showcase becomes credible when its citizens, places, and systems have explicit identities and honest implementation boundaries.
demonstrations.whatItProves: The routed Digitens experience, current catalog-backed city information, and a visitor-facing explanation of the living-world architecture.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: Autonomous Digiten behavior, persistent city simulation, production Renderer integration, or fully simulated transport and commerce.
demonstrations.runInstructions: Open /digitens in this WebPage checkout. The page distinguishes current data and demonstrations from systems that remain planned.
demonstrations.requirements: No special browser capability is required.

demonstrations.title: Singularity City Lab — Three Skins and Historical Eras
demonstrations.summary: Inspect a city-generation planning surface with selectable visual skins and historical/speculative eras.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: The same spatial identity can support multiple presentations without confusing visual style with world data.
demonstrations.whatItProves: A visitor can inspect the authored city model across visual treatments and historical/speculative framing.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: A historically complete city model, a live procedural urban simulation, or production Renderer integration.
demonstrations.runInstructions: Open /city-lab in this WebPage checkout. Future-era chapters are explicitly fictional planning scenarios.
demonstrations.requirements: No special browser capability is required.

demonstrations.title: Soldier Field — Exoskeleton and Event Horizon Lab
demonstrations.summary: Inspect an original science-fiction exoskeleton trooper, select semantic parts, derive preliminary engineering cut sheets, and scale independent per-horizon GPU workloads.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: Stable semantic part records can feed the rendered soldier, cut sheets, future research boards, and geometry-quality variants from one source of truth.
demonstrations.status: Live WebPage experience — exploratory WebGPU lab
demonstrations.whatItProves: A same-origin WebGPU geometry lab with 38 stable semantic part records, a versioned engineering-data schema, downloadable data-derived cut sheets, and per-horizon stress telemetry.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: Certified BIM, fabrication-ready geometry, production Renderer bucket integration, pixel-accurate obstruction handling, GPU timestamp measurements, or controlled performance gains.
demonstrations.runInstructions: Open the embedded lab in a browser with WebGPU support. Inspect semantic parts and download preliminary JSON cut sheets. Population controls are a stress harness, not physical occupancy.
demonstrations.requirements: A browser with WebGPU support. Part data are preliminary and are not manufacturing instructions.

demonstrations.title: Physics Replay Lab — Shareable Moments Prototype
demonstrations.summary: Scrub a bounded illustrative timeline, inspect event markers, and revisit a highlighted instant in the browser.
demonstrations.whyItMatters: The Workshop needs a visible route from deterministic history to inspectable moments while keeping physical reconstruction and portable sharing honest.
demonstrations.status: Runnable WebPage experience — illustrative fixture only
demonstrations.whatItProves: The local browser fixture supports timeline scrubbing, step/play controls, event-ledger inspection, and a clear distinction between available UI and future Physics integration.
demonstrations.whatItDoesNotProve: It does not consume Physics checkpoints, reconstruct a solver/world, establish deterministic physical replay, or implement portable moments, sharing, hosting, or remix.
demonstrations.runInstructions: Open /replay-lab in this WebPage checkout. The timeline is deterministic fixture data; it is not generated by the Physics world-replay executor.
demonstrations.requirements: No special browser capability is required. A local WebPage checkout is required to run the route.
